note: What the canned page answers, as a real run of its prompt would have recorded it. The page is fixtures/canned-page.html, the prompt the bench's own 'standup' first build; its three assertions pass on it — it names Yesterday, Today and Blockers, it reads its data through the bridge and it holds an add form — which is what a fixture author reads off the page and commits, the way the dictation fixtures commit their reference transcripts. The turns and the wall time are the fixture's own numbers, never a measurement: a dry run measures the machine, the harness it would draw in and the warnings the page was written with, and labels everything else as the fixture's. A real run replaces all of it.

assertions.name: the page names the three standup parts
the page's data bridge answers a read
the page has a way to add a standup
